Chapter 101: 0098 The Opera Girl's Way of Expression

Chen Guiliang walked out whistling, a bath towel wrapped around his waist.

He was in a very good mood, even a little giddy, perhaps because of the alcohol.

When Chen Guiliang returned to the room, Bian Guanyue had already put her ponytail up in a bun and wrapped a towel around her head, dressing up like a man.

"Dang dang dang dang… Clang!"

Bian Guanyue mimicked the sound of traditional instruments, suddenly taking quick, small steps and circling around Chen Guiliang.

Chen Guiliang smiled and said, "Which opera are you performing?"

He then saw Bian Guanyue stamp her foot and turn, tap the ground with the tip of her left foot, and send her skirt whirling as she executed the "deng bu" kicking technique of Sichuan opera.

Holding an imaginary folding fan in her right hand, she slowly traced a semicircle downwards. "Brother Liang, look at the water in this stream—murmuring, meandering from west to east, its course unchanged by rocks or sand."

Then her right hand shot up, wrist flicking rapidly as if fanning herself quickly. Her left hand, forming an orchid gesture, rested gracefully on her chest as she continued to sing, "If like fierce waves it crashed upon the shore, 'twould be naught but shattered jade and broken pearls, an utter void!"

After singing, Bian Guanyue took a step back and added an off-stage aside, "Alas, an utter void!"

Chen Guiliang scratched his head. He roughly understood. It seemed she was telling him not to be rash, that a slow and steady stream lasts longest.

Bian Guanyue sang a few lines as Zhu Yingtai, then switched to a duet in the voice of Liang Shanbo.

The impatient Liang Shanbo flicked his sleeve. "Worthy Brother, why speak like a pedantic old man? Ruthless flowing water is the most useless thing of all! See how the spring river's tide swells to meet the sea, only a thunderous rush can be called heroic!"

I've become Liang Shanbo, Chen Guiliang thought, and a very impatient version at that.

These lyrics must have been improvised, right?

Bian Guanyue took another step back and sang the off-stage aside, "Rumble, rumble, called a hero!"

Then, Bian Guanyue played Zhu Yingtai again, stamping her foot and reciting, "You… you're truly a piece of burnt charcoal! Hot in a flash, and cold just as fast!"

The off-stage aside snickered, "Hehe, a piece of burnt charcoal, oh my."

This line was spoken, and Chen Guiliang understood it perfectly: Bian Guanyue was afraid that things were moving too fast, that their love would burn out in three minutes.

Bian Guanyue once again played Zhu Yingtai, pointing at an empty space on the wall, "The clay Matchmaker ties the red thread, a lifelong bond entwined in a single strand. But Brother Liang insists on being like Nezha, tying the Crimson Luan to his Wind Fire Wheels!"

Chen Guiliang couldn't help but ask, "What do Liang Zhu and Nezha have to do with each other?"

Bian Guanyue gave him a captivating smile and swiftly switched to the role of Liang Shanbo. "Nezha wreaked havoc upon the sea, showing his might, his Universe Ring subdued the four oceans! Worthy brother speaks idly of slow work, I fear the Matchmaker is dozing off."

Chen Guiliang didn't know whether to laugh or cry. He played along with her performance, "Let me do the off-stage voice. It's too tiring for you to sing three roles alone. What should my line be?"

Bian Guanyue said, "Pretend to be the Matchmaker dozing off."

Chen Guiliang held onto the bath towel around his waist to keep it from falling, and shouted in a gravelly voice, "Time for sleep, snore snore snore..."

Bian Guanyue burst out laughing, then continued as Zhu Yingtai, "Fine, fine, fine! Since you wish to be Nezha, let me ask you: with three heads and six arms you raised hell in the East Sea, but did you ever ask what the Dragon Princess wanted? You haven't even kissed the Dragon Princess, yet you already want to go to bed with her."

Chen Guiliang understood completely now. Finding it incredibly amusing, he laughed heartily and sang the accompaniment, "Dong dong dong dong qiang, no you cannot, no you cannot!"

The hotel's soundproofing seemed to be poor. A man in the next room suddenly roared, "If you're getting a room, then get a room! What the hell are you singing at this hour!"

Bian Guanyue stuck her tongue out in embarrassment.

Chen Guiliang, however, wouldn't back down. He immediately yelled back, "What, you don't like us providing musical accompaniment? Take it easy, buddy, we're just singing a tune during our halftime break!"

"Psycho!" the man next door cursed.

Chen Guiliang found this hilarious. He ran over and closed all the windows, then said to Bian Guanyue, "Let's continue."

"Will we disturb others?" Bian Guanyue asked in a low voice.

Chen Guiliang said, "Don't worry, the windows are closed."

Bian Guanyue pulled off the towel wrapped around her head, letting her hair fall loose. She lowered her voice and sang, "Three years as classmates was not for naught, today I confess I am a maiden fair! I wish to entrust my life to you, but I fear your blazing fire will scald and break my heart!"

Liang Shanbo and Zhu Yingtai sang a few more duets.

Finally, in the voice of Zhu Yingtai, Bian Guanyue sang the words she wanted to say herself, "Oh, Brother Liang—twin lotuses must bloom in their own time, and green plums need years to ferment into wine. If you force me to marry you today, I would rather leap into an old well and turn to stubborn stone!"

Chen Guiliang stepped forward and pulled her into his arms. "I'm sorry, I was too impatient."

Seeing that he wasn't angry, Bian Guanyue's anxious heart finally settled. She said happily, "You haven't even officially confessed to me yet."

The mood was right. Chen Guiliang held her face in his hands and said, "Guanguan, I love you."

"Mm," Bian Guanyue responded, closing her eyes immediately, waiting for Chen Guiliang to kiss her.

In truth, she was also very eager.

Eager to taste her first kiss.

Their lips pressed together. Bian Guanyue was completely inexperienced and clenched her jaw nervously, then slightly parted her lips.

In less than a minute, she was out of breath. She broke away and gasped for air.

Chen Guiliang reminded her with a grin, "You know, you can also breathe through your nose."

Bian Guanyue, both shy and annoyed, punched him lightly and went to get her change of clothes from her backpack.

"I'm going to take a shower. No peeking!"

Chen Guiliang lay on the bed and closed his eyes to rest. He had gone to Tiananmen Square today, then wandered around Tsinghua, and then back to wander around Peking University. He'd also had quite a bit of beer in the evening. He was tired and weary, and he unexpectedly drifted off to sleep.

He didn't know how much time had passed, but he felt the bed dip. He subconsciously opened his eyes to see Bian Guanyue lying on her side, looking at him.

"Did I wake you?" Bian Guanyue asked.

Chen Guiliang smiled. "I wasn't deeply asleep, just dozing."

Bian Guanyue said cautiously, "I just feel like things are moving too fast. We only started holding hands while walking around campus tonight. The hugging and kissing, you just made up for those now."

"I'm sorry, we'll take it slow," Chen Guiliang said, reaching out to stroke her hair.

Bian Guanyue said, "You don't have to say sorry. I know guys are always in a hurry. When I was in high school in Rongcheng, I had a very good friend. The day after she accepted a guy's confession, he wanted to take her to a hotel."

Chen Guiliang changed the subject. "Those lyrics just now, did you make them up on the spot?"

"Mm."

Bian Guanyue picked up the backpack from the bedside table, took out a notebook, and said, "I wrote the lyrics while you were in the shower." She handed the notebook over, then suddenly remembered something. "Don't look at the previous pages."

Chen Guiliang recognized it. This was the notebook he had given Bian Guanyue last Christmas Eve.

The previous pages were likely Bian Guanyue's diary.

The open page, however, showed the lyrics Bian Guanyue had just written, with many corrections and revisions.

He hadn't quite caught everything she was singing earlier, but after seeing the lyrics, Chen Guiliang finally understood it all. The lyrics even had their own scenes and plot design.

Chen Guiliang said with sincere admiration, "Guanguan, you're so talented."

Bian Guanyue said, "When you learn a few operas, you have to memorize a lot of lyrics. You can just change them around a bit."

"It's really amazing," Chen Guiliang said.

Bian Guanyue was very pleased by the compliment. She leaned close to his ear and said, "My grandpa and grandma taught me Sichuan opera. After I switched to studying vocal music in middle school, I only ever sang opera at home. For so many years, besides my family, you're the first person to hear it. From now on, besides my grandparents, I'll only sing opera for you."

Chen Guiliang was deeply moved. He held her and said, "My grandma can sing opera too. When I take you home, you can sing with her for fun."

"Okay," Bian Guanyue said, even happier, her eyes smiling into two crescent moons.

Chen Guiliang kissed her again.

This kiss lasted a long time. Bian Guanyue felt like she was melting.

She pushed Chen Guiliang away and said, panting, "At most, we can just hug while we sleep tonight. You promised you wouldn't do anything else."

"Okay," Chen Guiliang agreed, though a certain part of him was very uncomfortable.

They lay holding each other and talking. Bian Guanyue began to talk about her childhood.

She never revealed her childhood to outsiders, but tonight, she couldn't stop talking. The sad, the happy, the boring, she said whatever came to mind, as if pouring out a decade's worth of repressed thoughts and feelings.

Chen Guiliang listened quietly, chiming in from time to time.

After chatting for a full three hours, Bian Guanyue finally grew sleepy. She mumbled while nestled in his arms, "You're so good to me."

Bian Guanyue said no more. Her breathing gradually became steady, having already fallen asleep in his arms.
